A poor scanned PDF (image-only) blocks go-live by failing every stage of the ingestion-to-reliability chain:

1. **Ingestion fails** – The standard PDF parser cannot detect a text layer in image-only documents, so text extraction fails. [NL-029#NL-029-S05] The parser returns empty document models or no text, leaving no content to index. [NL-021#NL-021-S02] This causes "failed ingestion of critical policies" and "incomplete text extraction." [NL-010#NL-010-S06]

2. **Citation anchors cannot be generated** – Without a text layer, the system cannot map text offsets or create citation anchors. [NL-021#NL-021-S02] [NL-029#NL-029-S05] TutorChat then either returns answers with no source citations, or points the citation to the entire document (e.g., "page 1 of a 250-page PDF") instead of the specific section. [NL-021#NL-021-S02]

3. **Reliability gate fails** – The go-live validation threshold requires 85% citation correctness. [NL-031#NL-031-S04] Because scanned PDFs return incomplete or incorrect citations, they fail this threshold. [NL-031#NL-031-S04] This is the explicit blocker: "scanned PDFs return incomplete citations, failing our go-live validation threshold." [NL-031#NL-031-S04]

4. **Manual pre-processing adds delays but doesn't fix core issue** – Workarounds (external OCR by the customer) delay onboarding by weeks (e.g., Northstar delayed pilot by 3 weeks, BrightPath onboarding stretched to 9.5 weeks). [NL-010#NL-010-S06] [NL-031#NL-031-S04] Without automated OCR, the system cannot process these files in volume, leaving the reliability gate unmet indefinitely. [NL-018#NL-018-S05]

Thus the chain: ingestion → text extraction failure → no citations/citation anchors → below 85% citation correctness → go‑live validation blocked. [NL-031#NL-031-S04]
